headline: Upheld condemnation order on alleged residential use of commercially zoned building at 580 Broad Street.
summary: The panel heard testimony from city officials, a health district representative, the appellant, and tenants about alleged residential use of the commercially zoned building at 580 Broad Street. The panel voted unanimously to uphold the Condemnation Order issued by Chief Building Official Rick Brown’s office.
decisions: Voted unanimously to uphold the Condemnation Order for 580 Broad Street.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr. D’Amato made a motion to uphold the Condemnation Order issued by Chief Building Official Rick Brown’s office. Mr. LaCart seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, with all voting members in favor and none opposed.

BUILDING CODE BOARD OF APPEALS 
Special Meeting 
Thursday August 13, 2026 at 3:30 PM at 
Bristol City Hall 
Council Chambers 
111 N. Main Street 
Bristol, CT 06010 
 
MINUTES  
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Acting Chairman John Lodovico called to order the meeting at 3:30 p.m. followed by the 
Pledge of Allegiance.   
 
2. Public Comments 
 
None. 
 
3. Discussion of Bristol Building Code Board of Appeals Commissioners and to take 
any action as necessary. 
Chief Building Official Rick Brown was sworn in and provided an overview of the matter 
involving alleged residential occupancy within a commercially zoned building located at 
580 Broad Street. 
Erica Mikulak of the Bristol Burlington Health District was sworn in and provided 
testimony regarding a complaint received by her department from tenants Jon Snow and 
Amber Doe concerning the conditions of the building in which they reported they were 
residing at 580 Broad Street. Ms. Mikulak stated that she was able to gain access to the 
unit and observed items indicating that the space was being used for residential 
purposes, including a bed, couch, small refrigerator, food, beverages, and other 
personal items consistent with someone staying or sleeping in the unit. Ms. Mikulak also 
reviewed the code violations cited in the Health Department’s order. 
Mr. Cohen, the appellant, appeared and questioned Mr. Brown and Ms. Mikulak 
regarding their testimony. Mr. Cohen also presented a lease agreement with Mr. Snow, 
which indicated that the premises were to be used as a music studio. Mr. Cohen stated 
that he had no knowledge that Mr. Snow and Ms. Doe were residing in the unit. 
Mr. Snow was sworn in and testified that he met Mr. Cohen in approximately 2010 or 
2011 and considered their relationship to be friendly. He stated that during the COVID-
Page 2 of 2 
 
19 pandemic, he contacted Mr. Cohen to inquire whether he had any available space for 
rent. Mr. Snow testified that Mr. Cohen had been aware that he was using the 
commercial space as a residence. He also described several concerns regarding the 
condition of the building over the years, including a lack of heat, bathroom conditions, 
black mold, lighting issues, and other concerns. 
Mr. Cohen questioned Mr. Snow and noted that Mr. Snow had not paid rent in 
approximately two years and that eviction proceedings were pending. 
Attorney Steeg swore in Jeff Arduini of the Community Services Department. Mr. Cohen 
questioned Mr. Arduini regarding his interactions with Mr. Snow and whether Mr. Snow 
had been cooperative when Mr. Arduini attempted to gain access to the unit to assist 
with relocation. Mr. Arduini stated that Mr. Snow was initially uncooperative but that he 
was eventually able to gain access to the unit. 
Amber Doe, Mr. Snow’s fiancée, was sworn in and testified that she had been residing in 
the unit with Mr. Snow for approximately one and a half years. She further stated that 
Mr. Snow had emails that she believed supported some of their claims. 
Following the testimony and presentation of evidence, the panel discussed the order 
under appeal. The three voting members present were Ed D’Amato, John Lodovico, and 
William LaCart. Charlie Talmadge was also present as an alternate. 
Mr. D’Amato made a motion to uphold the Condemnation Order issued by Chief Building 
Official Rick Brown’s office. Mr. LaCart seconded the motion. 
The motion passed unanimously, with all voting members in favor and none opposed. 
4. Adjournment. 
 
Motion to Adjourn at 4:48 p.m.  All in favor, none opposed.
